summary.title: DataPrep-Bench: Benchmarking LLMs as Training Data Preparators

details: LLM-driven training-data preparation (synthesis by LLMs/agents/workflows, and pre-training quality scoring) is compared only anecdotally: different sources, base models, and downstream tasks make it unclear which construction strategies actually yield useful data and whether any quality score truly predicts downstream gains.

DataPrep-Bench: a unified, downstream-grounded benchmark with two tracks under a shared protocol — (i) Data Construction, where methods turn identical raw long-form domain sources into SFT data and are scored by the downstream benchmark performance of a fine-tuned base model; (ii) Data Quality Evaluation, where any dataset-level scoring function is scored by Pearson correlation of its scalar against the measured downstream performance of models fine-tuned on the same candidate datasets ('quality' = downstream training utility).

Two released baselines: Data-Construction-Skill, a skill-guided agent that moves the specification of valid supervision (output schemas, sample types, filtering/coverage/validation rules) out of the prompt into a reusable skill layer while the agent plans over chunks; and Distributional Alignment Score (DAS), which scores a dataset by the negative MMD between its embedding distribution and an in-domain proxy dataset, motivated by domain-adaptation risk bounds.
Six domains: General Text, Math, Science, Medical, Finance, Law.

Construction sources: hand-selected open textbooks (Wikibooks, FreeBookCentre, Open Textbook Library) plus Chinese math textbooks/competition materials and IPhO/IChO/IBO materials for Science; 150MB FineWeb sample for General Text; all PDFs converted to Markdown via MinerU and released as shared input.

Downstream evaluation: MMLU-Redux (General); AIME24/AMC23/Gaokao24/GSM8K/MATH/MinervaMath/OlympiadBench under Qwen2.5-Math framework (Math); MMLU-STEM/Pro, GPQA, SuperGPQA, ChemBench, PIQA, SciBench under MegaScience protocol (Science); MedR-Bench, MedMCQA, MedCaseReasoning; XFinBench, FinEval-KR, CPA-KQA; LegalBench, LexGLUE. LLM-as-a-judge added for exact-match tasks.

Methods compared: DataFlow pipelines (incl. DataFlow-Skill composed via GPT-4o), direct LLM prompting (Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.0 Pro, GPT-5.2), ReAct-style agents in Claude Code (Qwen3.5-Plus, GLM-4.7, Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.0 Pro, GPT-5.2), and Data-Construction-Skill with Claude Opus 4.6.
All runs fine-tune jointly with Dolly-15k as shared instruction corpus; the Dolly-15k-only run is the reference baseline isolating the effect of domain synthetic data.
Base models Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B; LlamaFactory, 3 epochs, lr 5e-6 cosine, warmup 0.1, global batch 32 on 8xH20.
No cap on synthesized dataset size: each method emits as much as it decides (DataFlow 745K-849K samples; direct LLM 12K-56K), so scores combine quality and yield.

Data-Construction-Skill emits three disjoint QA types per retained chunk (concept, reasoning, case-application) with post-hoc removal of document-relative phrasing, duplicates and weakly grounded samples.

Candidate pools per domain mix in-domain and out-of-domain public SFT corpora (14 candidates for General; 8-10 for Math/Science/Medical/Finance/Law), with domain proxies Infinity-Instruct, ODA-Math-460k, Logics-STEM, ReasonMed, Fin-o1, DISC-Law-SFT (disjoint from candidates and test sets).
Ground truth: each candidate actually fine-tuned on three base models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.3) and evaluated; records released.

17 DataFlow quality/diversity evaluators as baselines (QuRating's four axes, Deita-Quality/Complexity, reward-model scorer, Superfiltering, FineWeb-Edu, PairQual, perplexity, BERT/SimCSE Vendi, MTLD, HD-D, n-gram, Task2Vec); per-sample scores averaged. LESS excluded as too costly and target-task dependent.
DAS implementation: Qwen3-Embedding-8B (4096-d), 5,000 randomly sampled instances per dataset, Gaussian RBF kernel with fixed sigma=1.0; wall-clock time also reported.

key_findings.finding: Adding LLM-synthesized domain data on top of Dolly-15k frequently degrades downstream performance rather than helping.
key_findings.evidence: Across six domains and both base models, most DataFlow-based, direct-LLM, and agent-based generators fall below the Dolly-15k-only baseline (notably in Math and Science on Llama-3.1-8B); since the only difference is the domain synthetic data, the regression is attributable to it, and surface-level quality proxies would not flag it.

key_findings.finding: DAS, a training-free MMD-to-proxy distributional alignment score, is the most reliable predictor of downstream training utility among 18 metrics.
key_findings.evidence: DAS leads or ties in 4 of 6 domains with correlations averaged over three base models, reaching r>0.93 on two base models in Math (p<1e-4), and is the only metric clearing r>0.70 simultaneously in Math, Science, and Medical; it is also ~1.4-1.5x faster than the comparable high-accuracy baselines BERTVendi and Deita-Quality.

key_findings.finding: No family of construction methods dominates: strengths are domain-dependent, and skill-guided construction wins in knowledge-extraction-dense domains.
key_findings.evidence: DataFlow-Skill takes the best Finance and Law averages on Qwen2.5-7B but collapses below the Dolly-only baseline on Science with Llama-3.1-8B; agents occupy most top slots in Math, Medical, Law; Data-Construction-Skill improves the Dolly-only baseline by nearly 20 points absolute on Llama-3.1-8B Finance yet trails the Dolly-only baseline on Science for both base models.

key_findings.finding: Existing quality/diversity metrics are narrow specialists and often sign-inconsistent, making them unsafe as pre-training dataset selectors.
key_findings.evidence: QuRating-Expertise performs well on Math and Science but collapses on General Text and Medical; Superfiltering leads on Finance yet is near-uninformative on Math/Science; BERTVendi is useful only on General Text; several metrics flip correlation sign across (domain, model) cells.

key_findings.finding: Finance and Law are open challenges for dataset-level quality prediction independent of the metric used.
key_findings.evidence: No metric evaluated attains a strong average correlation in these two domains; their candidate pools contain a single in-domain dataset against seven out-of-domain ones, compressing score variation, and their benchmarks test professional conventions poorly captured by generic text embeddings.
